campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 15, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered updates to the city's theater use policy, a cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose for resurfacing work, and the annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27. The Council also considered a budget adjustment to fund equipment replacement.
keyTopics: Proposed modifications to Council Policy Section 14 (Theater Use Policy), effective September 16th
Cost-share agreement with the City of San Jose, not to exceed $335,000, for resurfacing work
Annual update to the city's investment policy for fiscal year 2026-27
Budget adjustment to fund replacement of remaining equipment

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business, including approving prior meeting minutes, accounts payable, and an update to the city's Conflict of Interest Code, along with final map approvals for two residential lot splits. The Council also considered two appeals of Planning Commission decisions on residential projects and discussed law enforcement service options ahead of upcoming town hall meetings.
keyTopics: Final map approvals for lot splits at 20517 Carniel Avenue and 19351 Saratoga Los Gatos Road
Appeal of Planning Commission approval for a single-family home and ADU at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of Planning Commission approval for a three-lot subdivision at 14486 Oak Place
Law enforcement service options discussion ahead of September 19 and 30 town halls
Resolution amending the City's Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up routine budget and contracting matters, including updated employee pay schedules and additional funding for an electrical maintenance contractor, alongside several policy items such as renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street and restructuring the volunteer awards committee. The Council also considered longer-term topics including the City Manager's performance review process, a citizen zoning initiative, and the future of the Environmental Commission.
keyTopics: Revised Fiscal Year 2026/27 pay schedules for city employee groups (LAMEA, POA, and unrepresented staff)
A $250,000 increase to the maintenance agreement with Bear Electrical Solutions, Inc.
Renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Disbanding the joint Los Altos-Los Altos Hills Volunteer Awards Committee to form a separate Los Altos committee
A citizen initiative report on potential impacts to zoning and a discussion on the future of the Environmental Commission

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business at this meeting, including approval of minutes from prior meetings and the town's monthly financial report for July 2026. The Council also considered several contract and agreement matters, including amendments related to heating and air conditioning services and professional services agreements.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the September 1, 2026 Closed Session and regular Town Council meetings
Monthly Financial and Investment Report for July 2026
A first amendment to an agreement for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning services
Professional services agreements for the Town Manager to execute
A second amendment to an existing agreement

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 16, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed upcoming City Council agendas for late September 2026 and the public record for early September. The committee also considered approval of several City Council-sponsored special events, including a realtors' association meeting and car show, and took up a proposed policy on self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores.
keyTopics: Review and setting of the September 22 and September 29, 2026 Council agendas, including time-certain items
Approval of free use of the Janet Gray Hayes Rotunda for a Santa Clara County Association of Realtors event sponsored by District 9
Retroactive approval of the Santos Family Car Show sponsored by District 4
Retroactive approval of various District 5-sponsored special events
Proposed self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — September 14, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee met to take public comments, do a team-building activity, and consider its work plan for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Members also gave committee reports and reviewed upcoming agendas from other city boards and commissions.
keyTopics: Public oral communications
Team-building exercise
Fiscal Year 2026-27 Youth Advisory Committee Work Plan
Committee and staff comments and reports

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 19, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: This was a special morning session of the Sunnyvale City Council held for the annual 'State of the City' event. The agenda was limited to the event itself and standard procedural items for public participation.
keyTopics: Annual 'State of the City' presentation and event
Options for in-person, online, and written public comment

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 15, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met to discuss a closed session on potential litigation and property negotiations related to 10480 Finch Avenue, followed by a regular meeting covering routine city business. Consent calendar items included approving past meeting minutes, accounts payable, an ordinance on Audit Committee duties, a new AI use policy for the Council, and a response to a county Civil Grand Jury report on pothole damage claims.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation and property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with the Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of Cupertino High School students for their FBLA National Leadership Conference achievements
Adoption of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) City Council Policy
Appointment of Mayor Moore and Councilmember Wang to a subcommittee to evaluate city lobbyist proposals for 2027-2028
Response to the county Civil Grand Jury report on improving pothole damage claims processes

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Civil Service Commission — September 17, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara Station Area Task Force met to review plans for the area around the train station, including an update on the request for proposals for downtown development and the Fire Station No. 1 parcel. The Task Force also reviewed draft chapters on the vision, goals, and land use plans for the station area.
keyTopics: Status update on the Request for Proposals (RFP) for downtown development and the Fire Station No. 1 parcel
Review of Chapter 2 (Vision and Goals) of the Station Area plan
Review of Chapter 3 (Land Use) of the Station Area plan
Approval of minutes from the May 21, 2026 special meeting

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered several financial and infrastructure items, including the annual Community Development Block Grant funding plan and a proposed refinancing of bonds tied to the former Redevelopment Agency's successor. Council members also reviewed a presentation on the city's red light camera program and another on the current condition of the Milpitas Community Center.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution actions for the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency, including bond refunding and issuance

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — September 17, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Architectural Review Board considered a proposed sign program for the office property at 950 Page Mill Road, which would include a shared monument sign displaying the property's own branding ('Page Mill Labs') alongside identification panels for four tenants. The Board's role was to make a recommendation on the design as a quasi-judicial matter.
keyTopics: Master Sign Program for 950 Page Mill Road, including a monument sign with property branding ('Page Mill Labs') and four tenant panels
Determination that the project is exempt from CEQA review as an accessory structure
